name: Black Sabbath
hook: A Birmingham blues band whose guitarist lost his fingertips in a factory, tuned his guitar down to make it playable, and in doing so set the sound of heavy metal.
blurb: Black Sabbath formed in Birmingham, an industrial city in England, in 1968: Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler, Bill Ward and the singer Ozzy Osbourne. They started as a blues band, first the Polka Tulk Blues Band and then Earth, and in August 1969 renamed themselves after a horror film showing near their rehearsal room. Iommi had lost the tips of two fingers in an accident at the sheet-metal factory where he worked. To make playing hurt less, he tuned his guitar lower. That low, heavy sound, played slowly, with a creepy, clashing interval called the tritone in the title track of their first album, was far darker than the blues bands they came from. The album came out on Vertigo on Friday 13 February 1970 and reached number eight in the UK, and 'Paranoid' followed the same year. They are generally credited as the first heavy metal band. Others have a claim too (Led Zeppelin, Deep Purple, Blue Cheer), but it holds best for the low, slow sound that doom metal, sludge and grunge built on. They were active from 1968 to 2006 and 2011 to 2017, and played a final reunion show at Villa Park in Birmingham on 5 July 2025. Osbourne died seventeen days later.
